ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Emily Dickinson — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Home visit for the three-month kidney and blood pressure review

text.paragraph: Three-month kidney and blood pressure review at home. [S]

Ms. Dickinson is seen at home six weeks after her gastroenteritis. The repeat metabolic panel planned for two to three days after the sick visit was not drawn: she felt better by the second day and asked the phlebotomy service not to come. After a nurse call she restarted losartan, dapagliflozin, and amlodipine on the third day, once she had eaten and drunk normally for 24 hours. She has felt well since. Her home blood pressure averages 122/76. She has had no headaches for six weeks, sleeps about seven hours, and is writing full mornings. She has had no ankle swelling on amlodipine and no lightheadedness. She keeps the sick-day card in her medicine cabinet. [S]

tr.td: Metabolic panel two to three days after the prerenal creatinine rise
Within days after acute kidney injury or a sick-day pause

Not drawn, a deviation from the plan: she felt better on the second day and declined the home draw, and the medicines were restarted after a nurse call without a recheck. No harm, judging by today's creatinine of 1.30 mg/dL and potassium of 4.7 mmol/L. Corrective action: after any kidney injury, the recheck is booked as a firm home draw before the clinician leaves, and the nurse confirms it was done before advising a restart
